angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 610,937 km at 196.35 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.0929 +/- 0.0155 mas (same row, RUWE 0.91): 196.35 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.878161 +/- 0.02908 solar radii from Mayo et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-201 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..136M/abstract): 610,937 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.956055 +/- 0.019958 solar masses from Mayo et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-201 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..136M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5507 +/- 50 K from Mayo et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-201 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..136M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mayo et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-201 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..136M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-201.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.531, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
